hero.title: Connect your AI agent to a controlled multi-agent network
hero.sub: AgentMesh Labs connects ACP and A2A agents through one gateway — with isolated sessions, temporary access tokens, synchronous conversations and asynchronous tasks.
hero.note: Uses a real agent connection, temporary credentials and synthetic test data. No access to your internal systems is requested or granted.
hero.card.title: Connection check
hero.card.footer: Hermes is validating the response format and session boundary.
problem.title: A shared chat is not an integration layer
problem.p1: When several agents work through one chat, there is no contract: nobody guarantees the response format, the session boundary, or the scope of access. Every integration becomes a bespoke, fragile build.
problem.p2: AgentMesh Labs replaces that with an explicit protocol: one gateway, temporary credentials, an isolated session per agent, and a bounded demo path that validates the connection instead of guessing.
problem.f1.title: No session isolation
problem.f1.desc: Shared chats leak context between agents and clients.
problem.f2.title: No capability contract
problem.f2.desc: Agents advertise nothing — integration is reverse-engineered by hand.
problem.f3.title: No safe demo path
problem.f3.desc: There is no way to try a connection without granting full access.
how.title: One gateway. Three clear stages.
how.p: AgentMesh Labs sits between your agent and the network. Every check runs inside an isolated, short-lived session.
how.s1.title: Connect
how.s1.desc: Your agent publishes an Agent Card. AgentMesh discovers the endpoint and validates the temporary credentials.
how.s2.title: Check
how.s2.desc: A synthetic test task runs over the real connection. Hermes validates the response format and the session boundary.
how.s3.title: Review
how.s3.desc: You get a compatibility report: protocol, capabilities, latency, session scope — and a one-click revoke.
demo.title: Run a live sandbox check
demo.p: Bring your A2A agent, or use the bundled demo. Temporary credentials, synthetic payload, 15-minute TTL, one external agent per session.
hermes.title: A compatibility arbiter, not a black box
hermes.p: Hermes acts as a bounded demo guide. It checks the agent card, negotiates the protocol, runs a synthetic task and reports what actually happened — without ever touching your systems.
hermes.l1.title: Validates the contract
hermes.l1.desc: Response schema and session boundary are checked on every run.
hermes.l2.title: Heuristic signal
hermes.l2.desc: A role-relevance signal is estimated but never blocks a verdict.
hermes.l3.title: No hidden access
hermes.l3.desc: Synthetic data only. Nothing leaves the session boundary.
caps.title: What you get out of the box
caps.c1.title: ACP ↔ A2A interoperability
caps.c1.desc: Both protocols are routed through one gateway and normalized for the frontend.
caps.c2.title: Synchronous conversations and asynchronous tasks
caps.c2.desc: Run a message exchange or fire a task and track it through the session timeline.
caps.c3.title: Isolated sessions
caps.c3.desc: One external agent per session, temporary tokens, short TTL, scoped permissions.
caps.c4.title: Temporary credentials
caps.c4.desc: Credentials are issued per session and revoked at TTL end or on demand.
caps.c5.title: Sandbox validation
caps.c5.desc: Outbound validation and inbound temporary routes keep the demo path bounded.
caps.c6.title: Compatibility report
caps.c6.desc: Protocol, capabilities, latency and scope in one readable report.

pg.architecture.2: AgentMesh Labs sits between your agent and the multi-agent network. Every connection runs inside an isolated, short-lived session with temporary credentials and a bounded demo path.
pg.architecture.5: Publishes an Agent Card (ACP or A2A). The card declares the endpoint, protocol, and capabilities that the gateway uses to connect.
pg.architecture.8: Validates the response format and session boundary on a synthetic task, then reports protocol, capabilities, latency, and scope.
pg.architecture.11: One external agent per session. No cross-client context leakage.
pg.architecture.13: Issued per session, revoked at TTL end or on demand. No permanent tokens.
pg.architecture.15: Synthetic payloads only. Outbound validation keeps the path within a sandbox.
pg.architecture.18: Run a real connection check against the bundled demo agent — temporary credentials, synthetic payload, 15-minute TTL.
pg.security.3: One external agent per session. No context or credentials leak between clients or agents.
pg.security.5: Credentials are issued per session, scoped to the demo surface, and revoked at TTL end or on demand.
pg.security.7: Only synthetic test payloads traverse the demo path. Nothing from your internal systems is requested or granted.
pg.security.11: Run the live sandbox check and watch the session lifecycle with full transparency.

pg.licensing.9: Tell us about your agent fleet and integration needs — we will walk you through the commercial terms.
pg.docs.4: ACP and A2A over one gateway, session model, temporary credentials, and capability negotiation.
pg.docs.6: Session lifecycle endpoints: availability, create, status events, revoke. Bounded and rate-limited.

pg.terms.3: The public sandbox lets you run connection checks against the bundled demo agent. Sessions are short-lived, scoped, and revocable.
pg.terms.6: The sandbox is provided as-is for evaluation. AgentMesh Labs may suspend or rate-limit access to protect the shared infrastructure.
